answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer: No, do not make up the miles. Last week was essentially a forced lighter week, and that is useful 8 weeks out, not a hole to fill. Adding volume on top of poor sleep, heat and a work deadline is how small aches turn into real problems. We pick the normal progression back up this week: long run goes back to 13 mi, and the quality session shifts to marathon pace, which is kinder in heat than threshold and more specific to your race.

new.analysis:
## How I read the week
Your pace, drift and heart rate all tell the same story: the running was fine, the conditions were not. On Tuesday you held your usual easy pace but at 153 bpm instead of 139, and drifted another 8 bpm inside an hour. On Wednesday the tempo reps hit the paces you wanted, but heart rate ran away from you and you were smart to stop. The long run was the same picture, pace steady, drift climbing, so cutting at 11 mi was the correct decision.

## Why we are not chasing miles
Four and a half to six and a half hours of sleep, a heat wave, a broken AC and a work deadline is a lot of load before you take a step. Piling make-up miles on top of that is the fastest way to turn a hard week into an injured one. The fitness from the last four weeks does not disappear in seven days, and we still have seven weeks of work after this one.

## What this week is for
The plan goes back to one quality session and the long run as the anchor, but I am swapping Wednesday from threshold to marathon pace. Marathon pace (around 8:35/mi for sub‑3:45) is slower, more race‑specific, and easier to execute when it is hot. If the AC is still out or sleep is still short on Wednesday morning, cut the pace segment from 4 mi to 2 mi rather than skipping it; the long run matters more than that workout. Run early, drink before you go out, and carry fluid on anything over an hour.

safetyCallouts.title: Sleep and heat are stacking up.
safetyCallouts.body: Four and a half to six and a half hours of sleep with a broken AC, a work deadline and summer heat is a real load before any running. If this continues once the AC is back, or if you feel dizzy, unusually breathless or your resting heart rate stays high, please talk to a doctor rather than training through it.
